Introduction One can argue that the Achilles’ heel of 3D printing is the propensity for processing- related defects to occur [1], due to the rapid cooling rates induced and thermal-cycling intrinsic to the process [2]
This is particularly the case for the nickel-based superalloys studied here; modes of defect formation include porosity [3], solidification cracking [4] and solid-statecracking[5]

Suchsusceptibilityisadisadvantagebecauseconventionalprocessing – involving investment casting for example – has evolved over many years to be a low and defect-free route with which 3D printing must compete [6]
